newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Third injunction against Brazil CVRD auction.
newsitem.headline: Third injunction against Brazil CVRD auction.

text.p: A third injunction suspending the privatization auction of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) was issued by another Brazilian judge, said a Planning Ministry official.
The injunction was granted by a federal judge in the northeastern state of Ceara, an aide to Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said.

The court case was brought by a group of lawmakers, headed by opposition deputy Inacio Arruda, which also includes deputy Paes de Andrade, president of the government-allied Brazilian Democrat Movement Party (PMDB), a Ceara court official said.
The aide to Kandir said the ministry was confident that the injunction could be revoked.
Two injunctions have already been issued against the CVRD sale.
On Friday, a Sao Paulo federal judge issued an injunction against the auction which the National Development Bank (BNDES), which oversees the privatization process, is already contesting.
Earlier today, a federal judge in the northeastern state of Maranhao granted an injunction also suspending the CVRD sale.
Up to 100 lawsuits have been filed in courts across the country against Latin America's biggest privatization to date.
Brazil's Supreme Court is due to rule later today on a second constitutional challenge to the sell-off brought by a lawyers group, the Order of Brazilian Lawyers (OAB).

However, the government is still confident that it can fight off all the challenges to the CVRD privatization and hold the auction as planned at 1000 local time/1300 GMT Tuesday. ((-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5511 2485412))
